Oracle Billionaire Larry Ellison Is Buying Up the Neighborhood
 
Plus, a custom-built home for under $1 million in Seattle and architects weigh in on the Kennedy Center
 
By Kerry Barger
 
 
JOYA DIGLIO/LUXURY AND LENS
 

This is an edition of the WSJ Homes newsletter, a weekly guide to luxurious properties, celebrity homes, interior design and the housing market. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

 

In 2023, Larry Ellison spent nearly $10 million on homes in a tiny gated community in Boynton Beach, Fla.—though they weren’t exactly for him.

 

The billionaire and Oracle co-founder, who paid $173 million the year before for an oceanfront compound in Manalapan, bought the properties for his family’s staff, including tutors for some of the five children he shares with his sixth wife, according to people familiar with the situation.

 

The purchases highlight how ultrawealthy buyers are quietly acquiring homes for household staff as they expand their own personal real-estate portfolios. Their employees live close enough to be helpful, yet far enough away to maintain the family’s privacy. Meta’s Zuckerberg, for instance, has bought a number of houses in Palo Alto to build out a compound for his family.

 
 
Jolin Ellison and her husband, Larry Ellison, watching the BNP Paribas Open tennis tournament in Indian Wells, Calif., in 2022. MARCIO JOSE SANCHEZ/AP
 

Caryn Buck and Andy Thomas had lived in their Seattle Colonial for 30 years when they decided it was time to downsize. In 2022, they paid $1 million for a rundown, circa-1940 house on a 3,000-square-foot lot in Madison Park, but rather than putting an addition on the house, they started from scratch.

 

It wasn’t easy to stay within their construction budget of just under $1 million while maintaining high quality, according to their architect Sarah Smith. “It’s a constant battle,” she said. “You have to be creative and realistic.”

 
 
 

The Gated Community Where Larry Ellison Bought Eight Homes for His Staff

 
 
JOYA DIGLIO/LUXURY AND LENS
 

The Oracle billionaire spent almost $10 million on houses for his children’s tutors and others about 30 minutes from his Florida compound.

 
 
 
CONTENT FROM: ONE PARK
 
 
A Landmark Address along Florida’s Gulf Coast
 
One Park Sarasota was envisioned as far more than a collection of luxury homes—it was thoughtfully designed as a landmark address that elevates everyday living. Each residence captures breathtaking panoramic views, complemented by more than 40,000 square feet of resort-style amenities, impeccably curated finishes, and artisanal craftsmanship that reflects uncompromising attention to detail.
 
SCHEDULE A PRESENTATION TODAY  >
 
 
 

Two Seattle Grandparents Sacrificed Space to Build a Home for Under $1 Million

 
 
EIRIK JOHNSON FOR WSJ
 

To stick to their budget, the couple ditched a third bedroom and turned the second floor into a multipurpose space for their grandkids.

 
 
 

What’s the Deal?

 
 
SIMON BERLYN
 

Casa Encantada changed hands for $130 million in July in an auction. The winning bidder, whose identity has remained a tightly held secret, was a limited liability company with ties to technology billionaire Peter Thiel.

 

Media mogul Tyler Perry is listing his 22.5-acre California estate, which housed Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, when they first moved to the U.S. in 2020. The asking price is $57 million.

 

Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison is relisting his roughly 8.4-acre North Palm Beach property for $165 million—14% more than his original asking price in 2022.

 

British billionaire Chris Rokos has sold his mansion in the affluent Palm Beach County town of Manalapan, Fla., for $83.2 million. The unidentified buyer likely views the property, which sits on close to 3 acres, as a prospective teardown or renovation project.

 

Want to see more deals? Sign up for our Mansion Deals email alert to have the biggest and best luxury home sales and listings delivered to your inbox.

 
 
 

The Luxe Life

 
 
AARON SCHWARTZ/REUTERS
 

Architects were alarmed after President Trump said he might demolish the Kennedy Center. Designed by Edward Durell Stone, the building was never a favorite, they said, but it shouldn’t be destroyed.

 

Built by a General Motors executive, a 1920s Ann Arbor, Mich., property once housed Jersey cattle and produced its own branded milk for neighbors. It is asking $3.5 million.

 

Zoe Kazan avoided the 1955 film “East of Eden,” directed by her grandfather, Elia Kazan, while she was writing the Netflix miniseries. “My version is very different from his, but he was on my mind.”

 
 
 

House of the Week

 
 
CRISTIAN CRUZIO
 

WSJ’s House of the Week brings us to Venice, Calif., where an artificial-intelligence startup co-founder built a wellness sanctuary with a sauna, steam room and cold plunge in his backyard.

 

“I wanted this to be almost like the yin to the yang,” Akash Nigam says. “If you were just coming off Abbot Kinney Boulevard, which is action-packed, you could immediately enter this Zen arena.”

 
 
 

Your Home

 

• House hunters face a financial double whammy rarely seen: rapidly rising mortgage rates and home prices that, while growing more slowly, keep hitting record highs.

 

• NorthPoint Development offered $10,000 to each of the 4,500 households in Hazle Township, Pa., to allow a new data-center project.

 

• Mortgage rates posted their largest increase in four years this week, one of the clearest signs of how the recent bond-market selloff is spilling into the broader economy.
